content.comment_body: Hello - After waiting for some time, I have finally received my [product_name]. Previously, I tried ordering from Germany, but the distributor wouldn’t sell to a US address. After loading my program, I see status messages online, but I am unable to access the Parameters section to make changes. Is there something I’m missing, or is it not possible? I tried both Chrome and a tablet, but had the same results. Any suggestions would be helpful! Thank you, [user_name].

Hi, Changing parameters through the web server is possible. Please check the message text to see if protection is enabled. If protection is active, you won’t be able to modify any parameters. Hope this helps.

Thank you for your response. I reviewed all the message texts and disabled protection on a few, but still can’t access the menu screen. On my [product_name], I scroll through active messages to the date, then press ESC to enter the menu. This doesn’t seem to work via the webserver—I can’t scroll beyond the lowest message, and pressing ESC just toggles the LEFT/RIGHT buttons between dark and light. When they appear dark, the UP/DOWN buttons also don’t respond (I see them 'flash' when pressed, but nothing happens). Also, the softkeys set to start ON aren’t active after uploading the program (they do retain their settings after powering up). Please see screenshot. Thanks again! [user_name]
The program I’m using was originally for a [article_no] device and then adapted for a [article_no]. I’m now creating a fresh test program to see if that resolves the issue. Thanks.
To change parameters via the web server, create a message text block with editable parameters. When this message appears on the web server, double-click the relevant parameters to adjust them.

Thank you very much! For example, to set a weekly timer, I used the F1 key to bring up the timer in a message, then clicked the value to change it. This process works smoothly. I initially thought on-screen navigation would be just like pressing buttons on the physical device and that I’d have to access MENU > PARAMETER to make adjustments. This workflow is much simpler for my customers, making changes easier. Thanks again! [user_name]
Thanks—now I understand all changes need to be done via messages. I assumed users could access menus just like on the actual keypad. Appreciate the clarification! [user_name]
Final question: Is there a tutorial for the webserver functions available? Thanks, [user_name]
Everything is covered in the manual. [url]
A new question posted by [user_name] has been moved to a dedicated thread titled Help with web server, modify an output. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Initially, the user expected the web server navigation to work like using the device's physical controls, enabling changes via the menu just as on the keypad. The conversation clarified that only message text blocks allow parameter changes on the web interface, whereas direct menu access isn’t available remotely. Once this was understood, the user recognized that editing via messages on the web server could actually be more user-friendly for end customers.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wanted to use the web server to interact with the device in the same way as the physical interface, expecting to modify parameters through the on-screen menu system just like with the device keypad.
